item.title: Question about dummy coding categorical variables for a GLM in R
item.description:
Hi,
I am trying to run a negative binomial GLM in R with two categorical predictors. I seem to get vastly different results for one of the categories depending on which level is set as the reference. The categories are sex and phenotype. When I set female as the reference level for the model I get the following results:
``` Call: glm.nb(formula = substitute(i ~ Sex * Pheno, list(i = as.name(x))), data = GLM, init.theta = 1.992601217, link = log)
Coefficients: Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|) (Intercept) 6.9578 0.1720 40.457 < 2e-16 *** SexM 0.8074 0.2432 3.321 0.000898 *** PhenoA 0.9601 0.2267 4.234 2.29e-05 *** SexM:PhenoA -0.5649 0.3324 -1.699 0.089228 . --- Signif. codes: 0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
(Dispersion parameter for Negative Binomial(1.9926) family taken to be 1)
Null deviance: 104.192 on 73 degrees of freedom Residual deviance: 80.039 on 70 degrees of freedom AIC: 1283.3
Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 1
Theta: 1.993 Std. Err.: 0.305
2 x log-likelihood: -1273.330
```
When I set the reference to male I get the following
``` Call: glm.nb(formula = substitute(i ~ Sex * Pheno, list(i = as.name(x))), data = GLM, init.theta = 1.992601217, link = log)
Coefficients: Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|) (Intercept) 7.7652 0.1719 45.176 < 2e-16 *** SexF -0.8074 0.2432 -3.321 0.000898 *** PhenoA 0.3952 0.2431 1.626 0.103967 SexF:PhenoA 0.5649 0.3324 1.699 0.089228 . --- Signif. codes: 0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
(Dispersion parameter for Negative Binomial(1.9926) family taken to be 1)
Null deviance: 104.192 on 73 degrees of freedom Residual deviance: 80.039 on 70 degrees of freedom AIC: 1283.3
Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 1
Theta: 1.993 Std. Err.: 0.305
2 x log-likelihood: -1273.330 ```
The sign of the coefficient for sex is inverted which is expected, but the coefficient for phenotype is vastly different, as is the Z score and p value. Can someone please explain why this? Thank you.
